title: upgrade attention kernels to FlashAttentionV2 with fused ops and rotary (rope) optimizations
author: Sana Park
description: Summary: Replace existing attention microkernel with a FlashAttentionV2-based implementation and introduce a set of fused operator paths (fused qkv, fused rotary/rope application, and fused softmax + dropout reduction) to improve throughput and reduce memory pressure for long-context workloads. Motivation: Several production workloads (chat assistants and long-context embeddings) were suffering from tail latency and high memory usage due to multiple read/write passes during attention. FlashAttentionV2 provides more efficient attention kernel shapes and memory access patterns; combined with fused ops we can avoid intermediate allocations and extra kernel launches. Changes include: - New C++/CUDA kernels under runtime/attention/flash_v2/* implementing FlashAttentionV2 with optional fused QKV interleave and fused rotary embedding application. - A lightweight dispatcher that picks the best kernel variant at runtime based on model dtype, sequence length, head size, and GPU capabilities (compute capability and available shared memory). - Integration with the KV cache manager to expose an in-place KV layout that avoids costly copies for saved key/value tensors when using the fused layout. - Compiler/CMake flags and build shims to enable the new kernels only when the target toolchain supports the required CUDA features; graceful fallback to legacy path otherwise. - Unit and integration tests (tests/attention/test_flash_v2_*), and new microbench harness (bench/attention/bench_flash_v2.py) used for benchmarking. Benchmarks: - End-to-end throughput: +18-28% throughput on A100 for seq_len 2048 depending on head size and batch; +12-20% on 80GB H100 for common configs. - Median tail latency reduced by ~10% for single-request streaming workloads. - Peak GPU memory usage for KV cache lowered by ~15% in long-context LLM traces due to in-place KV layout and fewer temporaries. Backwards compatibility & safety: - Feature is behind a runtime feature flag ENABLE_FLASH_V2 (default on for supported GPUs) and a model-config opt-in to ensure deterministic rollouts. - Fallback path exercised in CI and included runtime detection for unsupported architectures; no change to network API or model on-disk format. Related work/items: - Linear: ENG-7643 (upgrade attention kernels), ENG-7890 (kv-cache in-place layout RFC). - Prior PRs: pr-32567 / pr-33210 which introduced preliminary fused-ops experiments. Checklist: - [x] Add FlashAttentionV2 kernels and dispatcher - [x] Add fused qkv + rotary operators - [x] Add runtime selection and graceful fallback - [x] Add unit + integration tests - [x] Add microbench harness and report results - [x] Update changelog and release notes Implementation notes: - The fused rotary implementation applies rotary embeddings in-register immediately after q/k/project to avoid writing full intermediate tensors. - We use a small autotuning table generated at build-time to pick the shared-memory tiling factors for a small discrete set of head sizes. - When ENABLE_FLASH_V2 is disabled or runtime detection fails, code paths route to the existing attention kernels without semantic change. CI and stability: - Initial CI run showed a flaky numeric-difference test in tests/attention/test_reference_comparison.py on a single CI worker; root cause was precision mismatch in an epsilon used in softmax reduction on FP16. We fixed tests to use relative tolerance and adjusted fused softmax numerics to stable reduces. - All CI checks passing on merged branch after fix (see ci_status). Merge strategy: squash-merge with a detailed squash commit message and release note.
